terms.gloss: small shears; nail scissors or clippers
evidence: Plin. NH 25.58: quod incīsum forficulīs, cribrant (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The diminutive of forfex, the shears that a barber (Mart. 7.95.12) or a vine-dresser (Col. 12.44.4) uses; often plural, like English “scissors”. The nearest classical tool to clippers.
Not in Lewis & Short: a tool-noun on resecāre, the verb for cutting nails (unguēs resecāre, Val. Max. 3.2.15; Traupman 58). Andresian is our only source for it.

phrases.english: Give me the clippers; I’ll cut your nails.

sources: Lewis & Short: forficula · Lewis & Short: forfex · Lewis & Short: reseco
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 58, 164, 374.
